/about/: Working to Provide Excellence in Psychotherapy in Dripping Springs Mandalas Symbolize the Transformation from Suffering to Joy My primary goal in working with clients is to help them find personal well-being and balance. When entering therapy, one may be unbalanced, traumatized, or hopeless. Our journey together will be one towards emotional strength and joy. I'm Leslie Tourish. It's Nice to Meet You. As a person who has transformed her own life, it's a privilege to be a guide for men, women, and couples looking to evolve the way they think and behave to lead a happier life. After earning a bachelor's degree in journalism, I worked for 13 years as a photojournalist for newspapers. A desire to get out from behind the camera and build deeper relationships with people brought me to a fulfilling career in psychotherapy. With a master's degree in human services from St. Edward’s University, I launched into learning from a variety of settings, including an MHMR clinic, a pre-release prison focusing on chemical dependency issues, a psychiatric hospital, and an adoption agency. Since 2002, I've been in private practice in Dripping Springs working with adolescents, adults, and couples. Fill Out the Information Form to Schedule a Therapy Appointment Issues I Work With DEPRESSION Everyone gets the blues from time to time. But depression takes a person down deeper, stretches out longer, and if unchecked, can be considered a medical condition. Gain knowledge about ways to manage depression. ANXIETY Our world can be an anxiety-producing place. However, a person suffering from an anxiety disorder may be under a persistent cloud of restlessness, sometimes resulting in panic attacks. Due to racing thoughts, they may find it difficult to focus and follow through in their daily lives. TRAUMA When someone experiences a terrible event, their immediate response may be to shut down with shock and denial. If the trauma isn’t processed, their emotional state may shift into mood swings, flashbacks, tearfulness, and extreme agitation, leaving them unable to move on in their lives. FEELINGS OF HELPLESSNESS If someone is in a state of helplessness, they may feel weakened, dependent, and struggling to handle their daily adult activities. This lack of agency may increase their belief that they are powerless to make the changes to improve their life, thus reinforcing their helplessness. FEELINGS OF HOPELESSNESS Hopelessness is a bleak emotion. Someone may feel that options are limited, if non-existent, leaving them with a deepening sense of desperation. SHAME This is a painful emotion in which a person believes they are inherently flawed, thus unworthy as a human being. If this belief is unchecked, a person could shut down and avoid growth opportunities thus keeping them more firmly into the self-sabotaging shame cycle. Explore Creative Ways to Solve Old Problems. Let's take a journey together addressing patterns and behaviors of your past for a more fulfilling tomorrow. 15 Minute Free Therapy Phone Consults Available Professional Experience After pursuing a career in photojournalism, I embarked on a journey of getting my Licensed Professional Counseling Degree. I benefitted from powerful training and learning experiences on the therapeutic process before entering private practice. During my earlier years, I worked in residential treatment centers, drug/rehab facilities, an adoption agency, St. David's Hospital Psychiatric Unit, and more. Working with clients in private practice has been my favorite way to make the biggest impact in people's lives. Leave a Review Many patients see great strides in therapy sessions with me and want to share their progress with the world. While I certainly love getting Google reviews, please keep in mind your information and however much detail you share is now public. If you'd like to leave a review on Google be considerate of your privacy first. /2024/02/06/as-you-think-so-you-become/: I often work with people who have had their trust violated, stemming sometimes from childhood when boundaries were crossed or basic needs unmet. My clients speak of these events as though they happened yesterday, although most go back months, years, and even decades. Yet as people speak, their emotions rise to the surface and they are once again caught in the perceived traumatic moment. And there's the magic word - perception. All of us have a unique view of the world, which is entirely our own. And it is our personal mental filter that gives life meaning. For generally happy and content people, life is seen as a fairly safe and reasonable place where they can solve most of their problems. But to anxious and depressed individuals, everyday mole hills can become mountains, and the world certainly is not a safe place to lower their guard. People's lives may be filled with many of the same features such as family, friends, work, and recreation, but the experience of joy or sorrow can depend more upon the person that on outside events. We may all know of the individual who, while monetarily wealthy, inside feels an emptiness no amount of retail therapy can fill. People, places, and things don't make us happy, but rather how we view these people, places, and things. Think about your own life. When you're feeling great, doesn't everything just seem to go along more smoothly? You have much more energy, you create and complete plans with enthusiasm, people respond more positively to you, and colors seem brighter. But when your mood turns blue, or even foul, the most simple task can become a burden and the world takes on a grey hue. Some of the reasons can be physical, but some can also be attitudinal. The ancient saying, "As a man thinks, so he becomes," really applies here. Often what we tell ourselves has a direct and powerful influence on how we think, feel, and act. Try an experiment. Tell yourself you're stupid, ugly, and life is unfair. What do you immediately feel? Now tell yourself you're smart, attractive, and exactly where you need to be in life. Can you feel the difference? the brain is like a reflecting mirror. It shines back exactly what you tell it because all it knows is your perceptions on interpreted events. As Man Thinks, So He Becomes. We are all born a blank slate - every thought, opinion, and attitude has been scripted by what others have told and shown us. As we matured, we were able to make our own conclusions about life based on those early foundations. So, if you were raised in a warm and trusting home, then you may view the world as generally a safe place. If, however, you were abused and rejected, then you may develop some emotionally crippling chains tied to fear and anger. But humans are powerful creatures! We all have the ability, through insight and hard work, to recognize our negative thoughts and turn them into positive feelings and actions. And, it may be as simple as saying, "I love myself. I am a good person. I am where I need to be." They're simple steps, but important ones to achieve happiness now, not sometime in the future. If you're seeking help on altering the way you speak to yourself to create a new destiny, I welcome you to schedule a 15 minute free consult to determine if counseling with Leslie Tourish will be a good fit. Please contact me today to schedule your free introduction.
